items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: PCF (Private Connectivity Fabric) NUMBERS AND THE BUILD-ECONOMICS DOCTRINE BEHIND THEM.

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: PCF (Private Connectivity Fabric) NUMBERS AND THE BUILD-ECONOMICS DOCTRINE BEHIND THEM. Q2 PCF revenue was ~$91M against the ~$13B of PCF deals announced to date; ~$36M of it was another STATE OF CALIFORNIA delivery milestone ACCELERATED into Q2 from the back half and 'now largely complete'. PCF CASH RECEIVED was ~$476M in the quarter and ~$300M of the ~$780M Q2 capex was PCF-related - and PCF capex is 'paid for up front by the customer', 'pretty much on schedule' with no significant efficiencies or risk found. CFO Stansbury: every PCF deal signed so far monetized CONDUIT 'paid for a quarter of a century ago' - underutilized assets - and created 'proximity with those hyperscalers'. On NEW builds, CFO Stansbury: 'the economics are a very different story ... There's great headline generating news in those, but the RETURNS ARE TERRIBLE. What I mean by that is that if you look at the cost to build new trenches, deploy new conduit, you're looking at returns that are AT OR BELOW COST OF CAPITAL levels'. Lumen's answer is to ride others' fiber: 'we're quite happy for others to build at or below their cost of capital so that we can provision higher margin, higher growth services on top of them.' A pipeline of 'fairly material' further PCF deals is in conversation, unannounced until signed.

items.reason: The Q1 PCF figure '$78M' is not stated anywhere on this call (or in the same-label release); only the Q2 ~$91M is. Removed the unsourced comparison. Verifier: CFO quote put back in its spoken order; editorial lead-ins removed.
items.evidence: Chris Stansbury: Second quarter PCF revenue was approximately $91 million, associated with the $13 billion in PCF deals announced to date.

items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: NEOCLOUDS ARE 'GOING LONG' IN 100G/400G WAVES

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: NEOCLOUDS ARE 'GOING LONG' IN 100G/400G WAVES. Strategic WAVES revenue (100G and 400G) grew nearly 11% YoY in North American enterprise, and strategic WAVES SALES were up nearly 35% YoY - CFO Stansbury called the sales growth 'a nice precursor to future revenue'. CEO Johnson attributed it to share gain, not market growth: 'the neo clouds go long in 100 and 400 gig'... 'Yes, we're taking share', enabled by RAPIDROUTES turning up circuits 'in days, versus what used to take months'; CFO Stansbury added that Lumen is 'definitely, I would say, taking share of Waves' because of its 100 and 400 gig routes and 'the density in those 58 million fiber miles that we're building, that are a big factor for the neo clouds'. CFO: there are neocloud deals in the $13 billion of PCF deals but 'They're relatively small'; CEO: 'Not as much PCF business for the neo clouds, but a pretty significant uptick in pipe and conversion of Wave capabilities' CFO Stansbury: 'That is a part of the Waves growth ... that's how they're choosing to buy their net connectivity'. CEO Johnson on the cycle: the uptick in 100G/400G is 'indicative, I think, of the SECOND PHASE OF THE AI ADOPTION CURVE, where more customers are starting to realize that they've got to upgrade their capacity', while legacy low-bandwidth wave circuits decline. Separately (CEO Johnson): 'data needs to find fiber as fast as possible. We do the backhaul for the satellite companies and it's growing pretty significantly'.
set.figure: 100G/400G waves revenue grew nearly 11% YoY, sales up nearly 35% YoY; 58 million fiber miles; neocloud PCF deals relatively small

items.reason: Speaker-labelled copy shows the '58 million fiber miles' line was CFO Stansbury's, not CEO Johnson's; the neocloud PCF remark was the CFO's ('relatively small') with the CEO's 'not as much PCF business' (no 'not conduit' statement); hedges 'nearly 11%' / 'nearly 35%' restored; editorial heading removed. Verifier: CEO hedge 'I think' restored on the AI-adoption-curve line; 'part of the Waves growth' is the CFO's.
items.evidence: Chris Stansbury: We're definitely, I would say, taking share of Waves because of the capabilities of our 100 and 400 gig routes and just the density in those 58 million fiber miles that we're building

items.label: Lumen Technologies Q2 FY2026 (08-04-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CALL-ONLY: MIX SHIFT, MARGIN MATH AND ALKIRA.

set.signal: CALL-ONLY: MIX SHIFT, MARGIN MATH AND ALKIRA. Total business revenue $2.44B (-1.8% YoY); North American enterprise (ex-wholesale) down only 0.2%; STRATEGIC revenue +14% YoY ('over 23% going back two years') and now 53% of business revenue, up from 51% in Q1 and 45% a year ago, while legacy fell 15% (CEO Johnson: 'Strategic growing 14%, legacy down 15%') - 'the mix shift... is happening faster than we expected'. Adjusted EBITDA (ex-special items) $802M vs ~$877M a year ago (mostly the fiber-to-the-home sale plus expected revenue declines); capex ex-special ~$780M; FCF ex-special $327M; special items $204M. Digital revenue $39M ('in line with our expectations as the category scales'). NaaS: total customers now EXCEED 3,000, new-customer adoption +22% QoQ with MORE THAN 20% brand new to Lumen (and, CEO Johnson said - 'I don't remember the exact number, but I think it's somewhere around 60%, we can confirm that offline' - of existing Lumen customers adopting NaaS were ADDING circuits rather than migrating: 'This is clearly a share take, it's not a one for one translation'), active ports +34% QoQ and active services +29% QoQ - all in a north-south connectivity market 'growing less than 1% per year'. The margin thesis: DIA ports are being made digitally discoverable so incremental digital services (Lumen Defender, DDoS, Multi-Cloud Gateway) can be layered on without a truck roll, and those incremental services 'are expected to approach 80% ADJUSTED EBITDA MARGINS'. ALKIRA closed in early July (not in the Investor Day targets; revenue immaterial today, positioned as upside) - a cloud-native east-west multi-cloud/AI fabric, nearly 4,000 Lumen employees already trained, most platform integration targeted within 18 months; proof points cited: Koch Industries multi-cloud hub setup compressed from 8 months to 1 day, Michaels connected 1,400+ retail sites to Google Cloud in weeks with no capex. Portfolio pruning: enterprise voice/communications products moved to END OF SALE (low-single-digit % of sales) alongside the copper exit; modernization/simplification savings on track for $700M exiting 2026 and $1B exiting 2027.

items.reason: The prior-quarter digital revenue '$37M' was stated only by the TD Cowen analyst (Gregory Williams), never by management - removed; CEO's hedge on the ~60% figure ('I don't remember the exact number ... we can confirm that offline') restored; the 15% legacy decline attributed to the CEO, who stated it after the analyst's question. Verifier: hedges 'over 23% going back two years' and 'nearly 4,000' restored.
items.evidence: Gregory Williams: Chris, you mentioned it was in line with expectations at $39 million. It's up only $2 million from $37 million last quarter.
